small_guidance:
- Add autotune configs that tile OC instead of materializing the full [OC, BLOCK_OH, BLOCK_OW] accumulator (OC=64 × BLOCK_OH × BLOCK_OW is large register pressure); try BLOCK_OH=4/BLOCK_OW=32 with the OC dim kept full but use num_warps=8/num_stages=3 and a config with smaller spatial tile (BLOCK_OH=2, BLOCK_OW=16) to reduce register spills.
- Switch the inner loops so that the IC loop is the outermost static_range and the (kh,kw) loops inner — this lets the compiler reuse the loaded x_vals for all OC weights more cleanly and reduces redundant input loads when KH*KW is small (3×3).
- Pre-load the weight tile [OC, IC, KH, KW] once into registers outside the spatial loop (it's only 64*16*9*4B = 36KB) and iterate output tiles, so weights are not re-fetched per spatial tile; alternatively cache weights via `tl.load` hoisted before the spatial accumulation.
large_guidance:
- Restructure as an im2col-style GEMM: one program computes a tile of (OH*OW) output positions for one batch with the full OC dimension reduced via tl.dot over IC*KH*KW. Use tl.dot with BLOCK_M=OC(64), BLOCK_N=spatial tile (e.g. 64 or 128), BLOCK_K=32 over IC*KH*KW=144, computing input gathers implicitly. Tensor-core dot will be much faster than the current scalar FMA accumulator.
- Fuse the channel-min reduction into the GEMM epilogue: after the dot produces a [OC, BLOCK_N] tile, reduce along OC with tl.min, apply tanh(tanh(x)) closed-form, store [BLOCK_N]. This avoids materializing the full conv output and keeps the min on-chip.
- Consider channels-last input layout (NHWC) so the K dimension (IC) is contiguous and the im2col gather coalesces; do a one-time permute of x and weight in forward (or cache transposed weight in __init__) to feed the GEMM.
